chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Banan ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, on the authority of al-Sakuni, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Muhammad, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his forefathers (peace be upon them).

He said: Six [types of people] are not greeted: the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian; the man who is in the toilet; those who are at the tables of wine; the poet who accuses chaste women; and those who make jokes by insulting their mothers.
ai.seo_question: Who are the six people that should not be greeted according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these six entities based on either their religious status (People of the Book and Zoroastrians) or their state of ritual impurity and moral deficiency (defecating, drinking wine, or mocking mothers). This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential nuance between greeting non-Muslims in their lands and the etiquette of avoiding those in states of *najāsah* or *ghaflah* (heedlessness). The inclusion of poets who 'insult chaste women' reflects the pre-Islamic and early Islamic context where poetry was a primary medium for public satire and social critique.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-16 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid -may God be pleased with him- narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quotedBanan ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Muqayrih, on the authority of Al-Sakoony, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his forefathers (MGB), “You should not greet six people: Jews, Christians; Magians; one who is in the toilet; those who drink alcoholic beverages; poets who accuse innocent women; and those who make jokes by insulting their mothers.”
